dedupe_keys.name: broadcasting resilience program disaster upgrades to abc radio transmission sites australia 2022 to 2025

description: This design and adaptation case covers a federal program to harden the ABC's emergency radio network after the 2019 to 2020 Black Summer bushfires. A Senate inquiry after the fires heard that 291 ABC broadcast sites were vulnerable in a disaster and that some, such as Walcha, Tenterfield and Armidale, had no standby power, while staff kept the Corryong site on air with batteries and generators; the Royal Commission into National Natural Disaster Arrangements noted that no communication medium is immune to failure. The Broadcasting Resilience Program then provided 20 million Australian dollars over three years from 2022 to 2023 to BAI Communications, the ABC's transmission provider, to add emergency power systems such as battery and diesel backup at 55 ABC Local Radio sites, backup programme feeds such as satellite inputs at 77 sites, civil and flood works at 10 AM sites, and five mobile broadcasting assets that can be moved to failed sites. The department reports the program complete, with 131 projects: 126 upgrades at 98 AM and FM sites and the five mobile assets. Coverage: national, ABC AM and FM sites in regional Australia. Format and access: program pages and ministerial releases, free. Caveats: no independent evaluation of performance in later disasters was found; site lists are not published. Simulation uses: adaptation options for broadcast networks under wildfire, flood and storm, backup power sizing and exposure of transmission sites. Related records: the Mobile Black Spot Program is a comparable Australian telecom investment.
